text: On every push to main, the CI job checks out the code, runs npm test, builds the storefront image tagged with the git SHA, scans it with Trivy, and pushes it to acrdriftwoodprod -- never tagged latest, always traceable to an exact commit.

The CD job runs only after CI passes on main. It authenticates to Azure using azure login with OIDC: GitHub issues a short-lived token, Azure AD trusts it, and exchanges it for a short-lived access token -- no stored client secret anywhere.

After setting the AKS context, helm upgrade --install deploys the storefront chart using values-prod.yaml and the new image tag. The same idempotent command creates the release on the very first run and upgrades it every run after.

A smoke test step waits for the rollout to finish and curls the health endpoint before the deploy counts as successful. But the pipeline never re-derives the autoscaling numbers in values-prod.yaml -- it just applies whatever is already there.
That means Lesson 4's minReplicas 10 now ships automatically on every single deploy, by design, without anyone re-examining it. Lesson 6 turns to the second half of the ask: AWS as a backup target.
